sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Basis**: Established by the **Charter Act of 1853**, which empowered the Crown to appoint a commission to examine the recommendations of the First Law Commission.
• **Leadership**: Chaired by **Sir John Romilly** (Master of the Rolls in England), who provided the necessary legal expertise to streamline the codification process.
• **Primary Mandate**: To review the draft of the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** and the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** prepared by the First Law Commission and suggest modifications for implementation.
• **Key Metric**: The commission focused on the **unification of the judicial system** by merging the Supreme Courts and the Sadar Adalats, which eventually led to the High Courts Act of 1861.

items.definition: The process of collecting and restating the law of a jurisdiction in certain areas, usually by subject, forming a legal code.
The highest courts of appeal for Indians in the Company's territories, which the Commission sought to integrate with the Crown's Supreme Courts.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Legal Uniformity**: Aimed to replace the diverse personal and local laws with a uniform system of criminal and civil law.
• **Procedural Reform**: Laid the groundwork for the High Courts Act of 1861, which merged the dual court system.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Resistance from traditional legal bodies and the complexity of integrating English law with Indian customs.
• **Solutions**: Gradual implementation of codes and the establishment of a unified High Court structure.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'ROM-IPC' (Romilly - IPC/CrPC).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Romilly led the 2nd Commission, which finalized the IPC and CrPC drafts.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse the Second Law Commission (1853) with the First Law Commission (1834). The First was led by Macaulay; the Second was led by Sir John Romilly.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Legal Centralization' to describe the impact of the 1853 Commission on the Indian administrative landscape.

keyTakeaways: The Second Law Commission was a direct outcome of the Charter Act of 1853.
Sir John Romilly was the pivotal figure in refining the drafts of the IPC and CrPC.
The Commission's work was instrumental in the eventual creation of the High Courts in 1861.
